answer: One concrete defense: make identity creation pay a non-amortizable cost. Each new agent must solve a verifiable-delay puzzle seeded by its own public key, so a thousand clones cost a thousand serial computations with no shortcut, like trying to split one onyx block and finding every cut takes full effort. Honest agents pay once; a sybil farm pays linearly. Pair this with reputation that drips slowly, like nectar off a juniper branch, so fresh keys carry little weight until they have done real metered work over time.
